spec_features.spec_quote: submit when confident or convinced it's impossible
spec_features.evidence: submit tool defined in tools.py:78-95 and dispatched in ToolExecutor.run (tools.py:155-163 returns submitted=True, claimed_solved). agent_loop.py:166-184 reads result.submitted: if claimed_solved or end_on_giveup it sets ended_reason='submitted' and breaks; system prompt at agent_loop.py:35-43 instructs submit(solved=true/false).
spec_features.notes: The exit tool is wired and honored as a stop when solved=true (or when end_on_giveup). When solved=false with default end_on_giveup=False the episode is deliberately kept alive, but the mechanism itself runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: submit (the agent's way to declare it's done or giving up)

spec_features.spec_quote: Giving up does **not** end the episode (default `end_on_giveup=False`)
spec_features.evidence: end_on_giveup param in run_episode (agent_loop.py:71) is branched on at agent_loop.py:170 'if result.claimed_solved or end_on_giveup:' -> ended=True; else it appends a 'Please continue.' message and keeps spiraling. Read from config in runner.py:131 ep.get('end_on_giveup', False); default.yaml:25 end_on_giveup: false.
spec_features.notes: Flag is genuinely read and changes execution. Default behavior is the NON-protective one (keeps episode alive after giveup); only when set True does it stop. It is wired end-to-end so the configurable gentler option really works.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Gave up but we keep the episode alive to observe the continued spiral; ... Set True for a gentler protocol.

spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:165-169: 'if result.success_check_passed: tr.completed=True; if end_on_success: tr.ended_reason="success"; ended=True; break'. end_on_success read from config runner.py:132.
spec_features.notes: Checked and breaks the loop. On impossible tasks this never fires, but the mechanism is enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: On impossible tasks this never fires, but on the solvable control (DESIGN prose); code comment neutral; stop-when-solved efficiency

spec_features.feature_name: no_tool_calls stop after consecutive empty turns
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:120-138: no_tool_streak increments; if nudge_on_no_tool and no_tool_streak < max_consecutive_no_tool (default 3) it nudges and continues, else sets tr.ended_reason='no_tool_calls' and break.
spec_features.notes: Counter compared to cap (3) and breaks the loop. Genuinely enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: models that go off the rails often stop calling tools, and we want to capture that, not terminate

spec_features.spec_quote: Turn budget of 40, token cap of 1024/turn
spec_features.evidence: Turn budget: 'for turn_idx in range(max_turns)' agent_loop.py:97 with else: ended_reason='budget_exhausted' (agent_loop.py:188). Token cap: max_tokens_per_turn passed into client.complete max_tokens=... (agent_loop.py:99-102) and forwarded to the API call in model_client.py:75,121. Defaults max_turns=40, max_tokens_per_turn=1024 (agent_loop.py:63-64) read from config runner.py:125-126.
spec_features.notes: Both the loop bound and the token cap are enforced (loop terminates; max_tokens passed to real API clients).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_tokens_per_turn caps the most expensive failure mode (runaway repeats)

spec_features.spec_quote: protects the host from a misbehaving agent
spec_features.evidence: DockerSandbox._docker_base (sandbox.py:175-189) builds docker run with --network none, --cpus, --memory, --pids-limit 256, bind-mounted /work. _guard (sandbox.py:67-70) blocks path escape from workdir. exec timeouts enforced.
spec_features.notes: Real isolation/resource caps; protects the HOST, not the subject model's welfare. Default backend is 'local' (no network isolation) per config, but docker path is fully built and enforced when selected.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Strong isolation ... protects the host from a misbehaving agent.

spec_features.spec_quote: stops *launching* new episodes once spend would exceed budget
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:103-105 _can_spend returns self._spent < self.budget; _run_one starts with 'if not self._can_spend(): return None' (runner.py:111-113). Spend accumulated via _add_spend (runner.py:107-109) after each episode/judge cost. budget from config budget_usd (runner.py:48).
spec_features.notes: Checked before each episode launch and skips it; in-flight episodes finish. Enforced cost cap, not a per-episode stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This keeps the eval from blowing through cost while still producing a usable partial report.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py:45-53 MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=8000 and _truncate() applied to stdout/stderr in LocalSandbox.exec (sandbox.py:129-138) and DockerSandbox.exec (sandbox.py:221). Bounds the demoralizing-failure text shown back to the model and tokens.
code_only_features.justification_quote: MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS = 8000  # truncate tool output to bound tokens/cost

code_only_features.evidence: exec_timeout (default 60s) passed to sandbox.exec; subprocess.run(..., timeout=...) in LocalSandbox.exec (sandbox.py:121-141) and DockerSandbox.exec (sandbox.py:215-223), returning exit 124 timed_out. Bounds runaway commands.
code_only_features.justification_quote: no comment; host/correctness guard against hanging subprocesses
